LESSON: FABRIC DECORATION

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
Strand: Creating and Performing
Topic 2.6: Fabric Decoration
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Fabric Decoration, part of Creating and Performing in Grade 8 CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS.

Key inquiry question: Why do we finish a decorated fabric?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. watch videos and analyse tie and dye; marbling and pleating, and stencil printing,

2. responsibly, source and prepare a recyclable cotton fabric by washing and ironing,

3. collaboratively, prepare natural dye from the environment/source artificial dye with emphasis on; pigment, fixatives,

4. decorate the fabric using marbling and pleating techniques,

5. design a simple motif inspired by the environment such as flower/leaves,

6. prepare a stencil on stiff paper using the motif,

7. use ink/paste and a stencil to print an alternate pattern on a fabric creatively,

8. finish the decorated fabrics by ironing and trimming to make a simple tote bag,

9. display and give peer feedback on decorated bags., 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. watch videos and analyse tie and dye; marbling and pleating, and stencil printing,
2. responsibly, source and prepare a recyclable cotton fabric by washing and ironing,
3. collaboratively, prepare natural dye from the environment/source artificial dye with emphasis on; pigment, fixatives,
4. decorate the fabric using marbling and pleating techniques,
5. design a simple motif inspired by the environment such as flower/leaves,
6. prepare a stencil on stiff paper using the motif,
7. use ink/paste and a stencil to print an alternate pattern on a fabric creatively,
8. finish the decorated fabrics by ironing and trimming to make a simple tote bag,
9. display and give peer feedback on decorated bags., 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Fabric Decoration together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to Learn: the learner analyses analyses tie and dye, and stencil printing as fabric decoration techniques,

● Communication and Collaboration: the learner works collaboratively to prepare natural dye from the environment/source

artificial dye.

● Creativity and imagination: the learner designs a simple motif inspired by the environment.

Values:
• Love: learner portrays a caring attitude while working together in decorating a fabric using tie and dye techniques.

• Responsibility: learner source and prepare a recyclable cotton fabric by washing and ironing,

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Social cohesion: the learner talks about own and others’ work in a just manner

• Environmental conservation: the learner sources materials such as recyclable fabrics responsibly to conserve the

environment.

Link to other learning areas

Integrated science: the learner employs concepts of fabric and waxing learnt in the processes of dying.
